sights.address: Stanford Ave & Junipero Serra Blvd, Stanford, CA 94305
sights.w: An iconic ~3.7-mile paved loop over Stanford's rolling foothills, named for the giant radio telescope dish on the ridge, with sweeping views of the Bay and campus. A local exercise ritual dawn to dusk.
sights.k: No dogs, no bikes; free street parking on Stanford Ave fills early on weekends. No water on the loop.

sights.w: One of the largest tracts of undisturbed marshland left on the Bay, with 15 miles of flat trails, boardwalks and superb birding along the salt marsh and sloughs. The Lucy Evans Interpretive Center sits at 2775 Embarcadero Rd.
sights.k: Flat and stroller/bike friendly; best light and bird activity at sunrise and sunset.

sights.address: 3160 N Shoreline Blvd, Mountain View, CA 94043
sights.w: A 750-acre bayfront park built on former landfill, with a 50-acre sailing lake, kite-flying meadows, burrowing owls and miles of paved trails linking to the Bay Trail. The historic Rengstorff House stands near the entrance.
sights.k: Boat and kayak rentals at the lake; Shoreline Amphitheatre concerts can jam parking on show nights.

sights.w: The South Bay's most popular open space: 24 miles of oak-and-grassland trails, the family-favorite Deer Hollow Farm, and the climb to Wildcat Loop and PG&E Trail. Open 8 a.m. to 30 minutes after sunset.
sights.k: The lot fills by mid-morning on weekends; arrive early or expect to wait.

sights.w: A 739-acre preserve of hayfields, oak woodland and orchard on the Saratoga/Cupertino line, with two lookout peaks (Hunters Point, Maisie's Peak) giving valley-wide views. A favorite of hikers, riders and mountain bikers.
sights.k: Only ~21 spaces at the Prospect Rd lot; go early. Trails are shared with bikes and horses.

sights.w: Santa Clara County's first regional park (1924): 1,077 acres of foothills around a 92-acre reservoir, with hiking, fishing, non-motorized boating and links to the Fremont Older and Skyline trails.
sights.k: $6 parking at the ranger station; a second lot near the reservoir is closer to the water.

sights.w: One of the oldest Japanese-style residential gardens in the Western Hemisphere (est. 1917), with a koi pond, tea house, bamboo grove and hillside strolling paths. A National Historic District in the Saratoga hills.
sights.k: Paid admission; the Lower House and tea garden are best in spring azalea and fall maple season.

sights.w: A serene 6.5-acre koi garden in Kelley Park modeled on Okayama's Korakuen, sister city to San Jose, with waterfalls, arched bridges and hundreds of koi. Free to enter.
sights.k: Inside Kelley Park; parking on Senter Rd. Combine with the neighboring Happy Hollow zoo.

sights.address: Naglee Ave & Dana Ave, San Jose, CA 95126
sights.w: A 5.5-acre historic rose garden with roughly 3,500 plantings of nearly 200 varieties, repeatedly voted America's Best Rose Garden. Peak bloom is late April through the summer.
sights.k: Free; on-street parking. Fragrance and color peak in May. GPS 1649 Naglee Ave.

sights.address: 368 Educational Park Dr, San Jose, CA 95133
sights.w: A quiet 33-acre passive park with ponds, a fragrance/sensory garden and the Chinese Cultural Garden, complete with a Friendship Gate and a towering statue of Confucius. Free and rarely crowded.
sights.k: Free entry; wandering pathways suit a slow stroll rather than a workout.

sights.address: 15350 Penitencia Creek Rd, San Jose, CA 95127
sights.w: Founded in 1872, one of California's oldest municipal parks: 720 acres of rugged canyon in the Diablo foothills, with mineral springs, stone grottoes, a creek and 13 miles of trails. Open 8 a.m. to a half-hour after sunset.
sights.k: Weekend parking fee; the Creek and North Rim trails give the best canyon views.

sights.w: The Bay Area's most famous foothill summit hike: a relentless ~6-mile round trip climbing 2,000 ft to a 2,517-ft peak and its selfie-famous survey pole, with 360-degree valley and Bay views. A rite of passage for South Bay hikers.
sights.k: Tiny Stanford Ave lot fills at dawn; overflow on Vineyard Ave. Bring water, no shade. Entrance open 6:30 a.m.

sights.address: 7281 Mt Hamilton Rd, Mount Hamilton, CA 95140
sights.w: A working University of California observatory on the 4,200-ft summit of Mt Hamilton, reached by a famously winding road with knockout views over San Jose. Free visitor center and tours of the historic 36-inch Great Refractor.
sights.k: Public grounds open weekends noon-5 p.m.; the drive is long and twisty with no gas or food. Check for construction closures.

sights.w: A 1917 Georgian country estate on 654 acres in Woodside, with 16 acres of formal English Renaissance gardens, reflecting pools and seasonal displays. A National Trust site open daily 10 a.m.-5 p.m.
sights.k: Paid, often timed-ticket admission; spring tulips and the holiday displays draw crowds. Book ahead.

sights.address: 21600 Big Basin Way, Boulder Creek, CA 95006
sights.w: California's oldest state park (1902) and its old-growth coast redwoods. Badly burned in the 2020 CZU fire, it has reopened for limited day-use with reservations; over 20 miles of trails are restored and the forest is visibly regenerating.
sights.k: Day-use reservations required; a summer weekend/holiday shuttle runs. Full rebuild will take years, so check current access before going.

sights.address: 101 Big Trees Park Rd, Felton, CA 95018
sights.w: An accessible grove of ancient coast redwoods near Felton, with an easy self-guided Redwood Loop, the San Lorenzo River and trails up to an observation deck. A gentler redwood day than Big Basin.
sights.k: Day-use fee; the flat Redwood Loop is stroller-friendly. The Roaring Camp steam railroad runs nearby.

sights.w: California's classic beachfront amusement park, home to the 1924 wooden Giant Dipper coaster and the 1911 Looff carousel, both National Historic Landmarks. Free to enter, pay per ride; open year-round.
sights.k: Free admission, ride wristbands sold separately; summer weekends are packed and parking is tight.

sights.address: 95 Kelly Ave, Half Moon Bay, CA 94019
sights.w: Four miles of sandy state beach on the San Mateo coast, edged by the level, paved Coastside Trail running from Pillar Point to Poplar Beach with wide-open ocean views. Day-use 8 a.m. to sunset.
sights.k: Francis Beach is at the end of Kelly Ave; the coast is windy and cold-water, more for walking than swimming.

sights.w: A horticulture-themed family park in the garlic capital of Gilroy, built around famous 'circus trees' and six gardens with gentle rides and attractions. Seasonal, open roughly late March through early January.
sights.k: Paid admission; low-key rides aimed at younger kids. Pair with Gilroy's garlic scene and the July Garlic Festival heritage.
